extracted.intended_audience: hospital financial officers, Medicare cost-reporting staff, hospital compliance officers, hospital administrators, Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs), and policy stakeholders commenting on the IPPS proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed Medicare/ IPPS policies and procedural requirements for (1) treatment of nursing and allied health (NAH) program revenues and allocation of indirect (overhead) costs on hospital cost reports, (2) related pass-through payment treatment, and (3) related payment/measure rules (immunotherapy payment adjustments and sepsis readmission measure adoption).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for deducting NAH revenue on Worksheet A-8 and treating resulting negative balances
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers must deduct tuition, student fees, and other NAH-related revenue on Worksheet A-8 prior to the allocation of indirect costs; providers should offset the total revenue generated by each NAH program, which may result in a credit (negative) balance on the corresponding Worksheet A lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This deduction prior to stepdown is consistent with Medicare cost-finding principles (42 CFR 413.24) and CMS PRM guidance. Example: Hospital A reports $1,000,000 direct costs and $1,200,000 in tuition revenues producing a ($200,000) negative expense on Worksheet A. The revenue offset ensures non-patient-care revenues reduce NAH program expense so unallowable costs are not passed to patient-care cost centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust accumulated cost statistic on Worksheet B-1 to reverse revenue offset for overhead allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure appropriate allocation of administrative & general (A&G) overhead to NAH cost centers despite revenue offsets on Worksheet A-8, providers must use the reconciliation column on Worksheet B-1 to adjust the accumulated cost statistic by the total amount of NAH revenue offset on Worksheet A-8, effectively reversing that offset for purposes of overhead allocation only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cost-report software providers must indicate 'override with value' and check 'add this value' to the existing accumulated cost (Worksheet B, Part I, line X). The accumulated cost statistic used to allocate A&G equals the Worksheet A adjusted expense plus the amount of tuition/fees deducted plus any amounts already allocated to NAH. The stepdown proceeds normally thereafter, while the NAH direct-cost lines continue to reflect the revenue offset so unallowable costs are not allocated to patient care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net NAH costs exclude patient care, related-organization, redistribution, and community-support costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Net nursing and allied health (NAH) costs do not include patient care costs, costs incurred by a related organization, costs constituting a redistribution from an educational institution to a provider, or costs provided through community support (per §413.85(d)(2)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restates existing regulatory language and is not changed by the proposal. Such excluded costs should not be included in NAH direct or indirect costs claimed for pass-through payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct cost assignment on Worksheet A must reflect costs 'directly attributable' to NAH education
rubrics_metrics.description: For Worksheet A assignment, 'direct and indirect costs incurred by a provider that are directly attributable to the operation of an approved educational activity' should be included; costs that would be incurred absent the educational activity (usual patient care costs) are not direct NAH costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a nursing supervisor who splits time between patient care and teaching should have salary apportioned between patient care and NAH cost centers based on percentage of time spent on each activity—analogous to apportioning teaching physician salary between clinical service and teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect (overhead) costs allocated only to extent they proportionately benefit NAH programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect costs allocated to NAH cost centers must proportionately reflect the extent to which the department benefits from the hospital's overhead functions; if a program does not derive benefit from a particular overhead function, it should not receive any of those indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal emphasizes proportional allocation (not categorical exclusion of all overhead). CMS listed typical overhead functions (e.g., Infection Control, Admissions, Patient Registration, Telecommunications) that usually would not benefit NAH programs, but recognizes operations vary; allocation must reflect actual benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Componentization (subscripting) of general service cost centers required for providers with approved NAH programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Hospitals with approved educational activities must identify general service cost centers composed of multiple overhead functions and create subscripts (components) separating (1) indirect costs that provide a benefit to NAH programs and (2) indirect costs that do not provide such a benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only costs in component (1) flow to Worksheet D, Parts III and IV, for pass-through reimbursement. For component (2) the hospital must delete (zero out) the allocation statistic on Worksheet B-1 lines 20 and 23 (and corresponding subscripts) so those costs are allocated to departments they serve but not to NAH cost centers. Example provided: A&G $100M split into $75M (benefiting NAH) and $25M (not benefiting); create subscripts (e.g., 5.01 and 5.02) and zero out allocation stat for 5.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish provider-incurred overhead from related-party overhead (nonprovider-operated programs under §413.85(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: For providers claiming pass-through costs under §§413.85(g)(1) and (2), separate overhead costs incurred directly by the provider from those incurred by a related party by creating an additional subscript containing related party costs; related-party overhead generally is not allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: January 12, 2001 rule clarified that overhead incurred by a related organization generally would not be allowable; under the proposal these related-party costs must be separated so only provider-incurred allowable overhead flows to pass-through NAH cost centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess clinical training costs removed post-stepdown on Worksheet B-2 for §413.85(g)(2)(iii)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any excess clinical training costs as defined at §413.85(g)(2)(iii) continue to be removed as a post-stepdown adjustment on Worksheet B-2, consistent with CMS Pub. 15-2, section 4022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This maintains existing practice for nonprovider-operated program clinical training excesses and distinguishes treatment from provider-operated NAH pass-through costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation statistics must reasonably relate to the general service costs and reflect proportion attributable
rubrics_metrics.description: The statistical basis used to allocate each general service cost center and its subscripts must reasonably relate to the general service costs and appropriately reflect the proportion of those costs attributable to downstream cost centers, including NAH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS refers readers to section X.D.3. for further discussion. Examples include using accumulated cost (adjusted to reverse tuition offset) as the basis for allocating A&G when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider responsibility to request MAC permission for nonstandard allocation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the provider's responsibility to request permission from its MAC to use an allocation method for overhead costs that accurately and appropriately reflects overhead costs incurred by the provider as a direct result of operating its NAH education programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This confirms that novel or nonroutine allocation approaches require MAC approval to ensure appropriateness under pass-through payment rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and cost report implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed effective date: cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2026; CMS intends to issue revisions to the hospital cost report (Form CMS-2552-10) to implement these policies if finalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers should prepare to implement Worksheet and cost-reporting changes for those periods and to follow any revised CMS instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude clinical trial claims from MS-DRG 018 average-cost calculation for relative weight when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: When calculating the average cost for MS-DRG 018 (immunotherapy/CAR T-cell therapies) used for relative weight development, CMS does not include claims determined to be clinical trial claims that group to MS-DRG 018; with refinements when the immunotherapy product is purchased in the usual manner but the case involves a clinical trial of a different product (such claims may be included to the extent identifiable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also, expanded access use of immunotherapy cases are treated consistently (not included when identifiable for the average-cost calculation in some contexts); distinctions affect both relative weight calculation and payment adjustments. See policy history cited (FY2021-FY2026 rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment adjustment methodology for expanded access, applicable clinical trial, and free/other non-purchased immunotherapy cases in MS-DRG 018
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed methodology to calculate a payment adjustor for cases that group to MS-DRG 018 and are (a) expanded access use of immunotherapy, (b) applicable clinical trial cases, or (c) other cases where the immunotherapy product was not purchased in the usual manner (e.g., obtained at no cost): compute an adjustor equal to average cost of targeted cases divided by average cost of other cases, then multiply the MS-DRG 018 relative weight by this adjustor when calculating payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: (1) Calculate average cost for cases assigned to MS-DRG 018 that meet targeted criteria (contain ICD-10-CM Z00.6 and do not contain condition code 'ZC'; or contain condition code '90'; or contain standardized drug charges below the median standardized drug charge of clinical trial cases). (2) Calculate average cost for all other MS-DRG 018 cases. (3) Divide (1) by (2) to get adjustor and apply to relative weight. For FY2027 the proposed adjustor is 0.17 (based on Dec 2025 MedPAR update) and CMS proposes to update adjustor for final rule using more recent data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of MedPAR condition codes and ZC payer-only flag to identify clinical trial / expanded-access cases
rubrics_metrics.description: MedPAR data contains fields to identify expanded access use (condition code 90) and includes a payer-only condition code 'ZC' which the IPPS Pricer uses to mark cases where the immunotherapy product was purchased in the usual manner but the case involves a clinical trial of a different product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will use these flags (and standardized drug-charge thresholds) to identify cases for exclusion/inclusion in average-cost and payment-adjustor calculations; see Change Request 11879 for operational detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt Sepsis 30-day all-cause risk-standardized readmission (RSRR) measure for Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed adoption of the Hospital 30-Day, All-Cause, Risk-Standardized Readmission Rate Following Sepsis Hospitalization measure for the HRRP beginning with an applicable period July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2027 (for FY2029 program year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: improve patient outcomes by informing stakeholders about hospital-level unplanned readmission rates after sepsis, encouraging evidence-based practices, implementation of post-discharge interventions, and appropriate discharge planning. The measure includes Medicare Fee-for-Service and Medicare Advantage beneficiaries. CMS notes measure statistics (mean RSRR ~18.09%) for hospitals with at least 25 eligible discharges using 2022–2023 data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of 'applicable conditions' for HRRP based on high-volume/high-expenditure standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 1886(q)(5)(A) of the Act, 'applicable conditions' used in HRRP (conditions for which excess readmissions reduce payments) should be high-volume or high-expenditure conditions as determined by the Secretary; sepsis is proposed as such a condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS references prior rulemakings and technical specifications (QualityNet) for methodology and measure details. The proposal aligns the sepsis measure with CMS's Meaningful Measures 2.0 priority area 'Seamless Care Coordination.'
